predecessors.name: Kanem–Bornu Empire
predecessors.text: the Fezzan, part of the Kanem Empire in the 13th-14th centuries and under Bornu rule 'by 1400' (Murzuk page); 'Wars against the Kanem-Bornu Empire in the early sixteenth century led to its founding'…

successors.name: Karamanli dynasty
successors.text: the Fezzan, 'occupied in 1811/1812' (Fezzan page) after Yusuf Karamanli 'brought the tribes of Fezzan under direct control' in 1807 (Awlad Muhammad page)

ledger.x: 1550: the Awlad Muhammad rule the Fezzan from Murzuk.
1639: Muhammad bin Juhaym overthrows the Ottoman bey.
1811: the Karamanli occupy the Fezzan and the dynasty ends.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Fezzan
wars.outcome: Ottoman Tripolitania under Mahmut bey invaded and occupied the Fezzan in 1574 (most African historians say 1577) and expelled Sultan Bulalah Muhammad; Bornu 'would aid them militarily against the Ottoman annexation'.

wars.name: Overthrow of the Ottoman bey in the Fezzan
wars.outcome: Muhammad bin Juhaym 'overthrew the Ottoman Bey in 1639, and assumed control'.

wars.name: Karamanli conquest of the Fezzan
wars.outcome: Yusuf Karamanli 'brought the tribes of Fezzan under direct control' in 1807 and the Fezzan was 'occupied in 1811/1812', ending the dynasty.

certainty.note: A Saharan oasis sultanate: no page gives a frontier; the Chad and Niger reach is not drawn.
